label: TP
reason: Both alerts are true positives. Alert 1 (java/xss): User input from request.getParameter() flows through doSomething() to response.getWriter().format(bar,obj) at line 57. Truncating the last character in doSomething() (lines 60-63) does not neutralize XSS vectors—attackers can craft payloads independent of the last character. Alert 2 (java/tainted-format-string): Same flow means user input controls the format string argument, enabling format string attacks.

evidence.note: User input param extracted at line 45, processed in doSomething() (lines 60-63), written to response.getWriter().format(bar,obj) at line 57. Truncation leaves attacker-controlled content in sink.
doSomething() truncates param by one character but does not sanitize special characters (<,>,/,etc.) required to neutralize XSS or format string attacks.
